    StartersEEV crash landing Scotch eggsSoft-boiled eggs wrapped in sage and mustard pork sausage, crumbed and fried goldenHow to make it5 eggs400g pork sausage mince1 tbsp sage, finely chopped2 tsp hot English mustard1/4 tsp black pepper50g plain flour80g panko breadcrumbs1 L vegetable oil, for fryingsea salt flakes, to tasteLower 4 of the eggs into a pot of boiling water and cook for 7 minutes.Lift into iced water, cool for 10 minutes, then peel.Mix the sausage mince with the sage, mustard and pepper. Divide into 4, flatten each piece in your palm and wrap it around a peeled egg, sealing the seams.Beat the last egg. Roll each wrapped egg in the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 170°C.Fry 2 at a time for 6 to 7 minutes, turning, until deep golden and the sausage is cooked through. Drain, sprinkle with salt and cut in half to serve.Mess line bubble and squeakCrisp potato and cabbage cakes fried in butter, with brown sauceHow to make it700g floury potatoes250g savoy cabbage, finely shredded1 onion, thinly sliced40g butter2 tbsp plain flour2 tbsp vegetable oilsalt and pepper, to taste4 tbsp brown saucePeel the potatoes and cut into even chunks.Boil in salted water until tender, drain well and leave to steam dry.Mash roughly, leaving some lumps.Fry the onion and cabbage in half the butter until soft and catching at the edges.Mix into the potato, season well with salt and pepper and shape into 8 small flat cakes. Dust with the flour.Chill to firm up.Fry in the oil and remaining butter over medium heat, 4 minutes a side, in batches, until crusted and golden.Serve hot with the brown sauce.Beef dripping toast with saltAndrews runs a tight mess line. Dice the onion, carrots and celery and crush the garlic.Heat the oil in a large heavy pan and brown the mince well, in batches.Add the onion, carrot, celery and garlic and cook until soft.Stir in the tomato paste and flour and cook for 2 minutes.Add the stock, Worcestershire and thyme and simmer, partly covered, until thick. Meanwhile boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.Drain the potatoes and mash with the butter and milk. Season with salt and pepper. Heat the oven to 200°C.Stir the peas into the mince, season and tip into a baking dish. Spread the mash on top, rough it up with a fork and scatter with the cheddar.Bake until bubbling and golden on top.Rest before serving.SweetsFiorina bread and butter puddingButtered bread and sultanas baked in vanilla custard with nutmeg and a crunchy sugar topHow to make it8 slices of day-old white bread50g butter, softened60g sultanas3 eggs300ml full cream milk200ml thickened cream70g caster sugar1 tsp vanilla extract1/4 tsp ground nutmeg1 tbsp demerara sugarButter a baking dish.
